title: Lighthouse Retail - access and cryptography review
topics: RBAC and least-privilege for multi-tenant hosted use
Audit logs / retention and immutable logs
Data residency and retention policy options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call focused on Lighthouse Retail's regulatory and ops constraints: they need SOC2-equivalent controls, SSO with SAML and SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, KMS BYOK for certain data buckets, and 7 years of immutable audit logs for payment-adjacent flows. Evaluating Redwood Hosted first but must validate Dedicated or Private for sensitive PII and data residency. Agreed to run a short security questionnaire and schedule technical pilot for KMS and SSO flows.

transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-08-30
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Daniel Herrera (CTO), Maya Lin (Head of Infra), Samir Patel (Security), Rina Ortega (Legal)

Summary: quick intake to map Lighthouse's security constraints and determine whether Hosted edition is acceptable or if Dedicated/Private deployment will be required for certain workloads.

[00:00:03] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Alex, AE on this deal, Priya is our SE who will handle the technical follow-up.
[00:00:15] Daniel Herrera: Hi all, Daniel here. We're evaluating inference providers for the new recommendation engine. Primary ask is compliance for payments-data-adjacent PII.
[00:00:28] Maya Lin: And I lead infra — we care about latency, but security is non-negotiable.
[00:00:34] Priya Desai: Great — we'll run through controls we have and where Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private differ. Can you outline your regulatory must-haves?
[00:00:45] Samir Patel: Sure. SOC2 type II is a baseline. We also have an upcoming ISO 27001 audit next year. We need SSO — SAML preferred — SCIM provisioning into our IdP, RBAC that can map to our internal roles, and audit logs that are immutable for at least 7 years for the payment checkout flow.
[00:01:05] Rina Ortega: From legal: data retention and deletion policies matter; we can't have long tail copies outside defined buckets. Also encryption keys — if possible BYOK, otherwise strong KMS integration.
[00:01:22] Alex Kim: That's helpful. On SOC2/ISO — Redwood is SOC2 compliant and we have our audit summary we can share. We also support both hosted and Dedicated where keys and logs are isolated. For BYOK, we integrate with customer KMS and HSMs — correct Priya?
[00:01:38] Priya Desai: Correct. We have a BYOK flow: for Hosted we support customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) using envelope encryption. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your keys on the instance or in a HSM in your VPC. There's an import/rotation procedure.
[00:01:55] Speaker 1: There's sometimes confusion about where model artifacts live — do they persist in Redwood object stores?
[00:02:02] Priya Desai: Models for hosted are stored encrypted at rest in our storage layer. We can pin versions and configure retention. For Dedicated we deploy model artifacts into customer-dedicated storage pools, which can optionally be in your VPC for Private.
[00:02:18] Daniel Herrera: For our use case we need model KV cache and transient tokenization buffers to never hit persistent storage for checkout flows. Can you guarantee ephemeral-only handling?
[00:02:30] Priya Desai: We support workload tagging and SLO-level routes — you can route payment-adjacent traffic to dedicated pods with ephemeral caches. Note that some telemetry needs to be persisted for debugging; we can scrub tokens and PII before storing and we can opt-out of telemetry for those flows. There is a slight tradeoff with observability.
[00:02:51] Samir Patel: About RBAC — we need least privilege across consoles and API keys. We want integration with our HR system so provisioning is automated.
[00:03:01] Alex Kim: We have RBAC that maps to roles and token scopes. SSO + SCIM can keep identities in sync; API keys can be scoped per project and per model, and you can rotate keys programmatically.
[00:03:12] Maya Lin: Do you map SAML groups to Redwood roles? Our internal groups determine read vs write vs admin.
[00:03:18] Priya Desai: Yes — group mapping exists. It's configurable. We'll show you a sample mapping in the pilot. Sometimes provisioning names are messy in exports — transcriptions left that unclear — but we do support group to role mapping and can sync via SCIM.
[00:03:33] Daniel Herrera: Audit logs — we require immutable logs for 7 years. Do you provide append-only logs and a way to export them into our long-term store?
[00:03:42] Priya Desai: We provide real-time audit streams and an archive export. For Hosted we retain logs for a default window (usually 90 days) unless you buy extended retention. We can push immutable audit exports into your S3 or GCS bucket with WORM-like settings for long-term retention. For Dedicated/Private you control retention locally and can set S3 bucket policies for immutability.
[00:04:03] Samir Patel: That sounds okay. We also need point-in-time attestations and cryptographic proof of integrity for logs for audit. Do you offer signed log manifests?
[00:04:12] Priya Desai: We can generate signed manifests for exports and provide hash chains for log batches for the pilot. It's part of our enterprise package; we'll surface docs.
[00:04:25] Speaker 1: Encryption in transit — TLS ok? We need mTLS for internal services.
[00:04:30] Priya Desai: TLS 1.2/1.3 is standard. For Dedicated/Private you can enforce mTLS at the VPC level. Hosted supports mutual TLS for specific partners if needed, but it's uncommon for self-serve. We can enable mutual TLS for partner integrations in enterprise setups.
[00:04:46] Daniel Herrera: Data residency — our legal team requires EU-only residency for EU customer data. How do you handle region parity?
[00:04:55] Alex Kim: We have region controls. Hosted supports model serving in EU regions. With Dedicated you can reserve capacity in specific regions. Private gives you full control. We'll need to map which datasets are EU-only and apply routing policies.
[00:05:08] Maya Lin: One more — network egress controls and private link — we need to avoid public internet for connectors.
[00:05:14] Priya Desai: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted has options for VPC connectors for enterprise customers to restrict egress.
[00:05:26] Samir Patel: About incident response — what's your SLA and notification process? We want immediate notification for auth or key compromise.
[00:05:33] Alex Kim: Enterprise contracts include incident notification windows (we notify known stakeholders within 1 hour for critical events). We also provide post-incident reports and remediation timelines. We'll share the SOC2 incident response appendix.
[00:05:47] Rina Ortega: Regarding contracts, we need to see indemnities and data processing addendum.
[00:05:52] Alex Kim: We'll send the DPA and standard enterprise terms. Legal can iterate.
[00:05:59] Daniel Herrera: Can we talk through an example flow — checkout hits our service, we call Redwood for a recommendation, we want no raw PII stored and logs exported to our archive.
[00:06:09] Priya Desai: Flow 1: Payment-adjacent route tagged; sent to dedicated pods with customer KMS envelope encryption. We scrub tokens client-side before log emission. Audit events for that route are exported to your S3 via secure transfer into a WORM-enabled bucket. We can also session-isolate the KV cache so it's memory-only and never flushed to disk for those routes.
[00:06:31] Daniel Herrera: You said session isolate — is that configurable per route today?
[00:06:35] Priya Desai: Yes. Routing policies can be per-route with policies for cache persistence, tracing, and telemetry. There is small overhead for isolation but it's usually acceptable for low-volume critical flows.
[00:06:49] Maya Lin: What about keys — do you have a KMS rotation schedule or do we manage rotation?
[00:06:54] Priya Desai: With BYOK you manage rotation within your KMS; Redwood honors key versions and key identifiers. For Hosted where keys are in our managed KMS, we rotate keys per best practices but you can request rotation policies. For Dedicated you fully control lifecycle.
[00:07:10] Samir Patel: Any limitations on HSMs or FIPS 140-2 requirements?
[00:07:15] Priya Desai: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs in supported clouds; for air-gapped/HSM-on-prem we typically recommend Private deployment.
[00:07:26] Speaker 1: Are there any regulatory gaps you’ve seen with other customers who moved from Hosted to Dedicated?
[00:07:31] Alex Kim: Common gap is telemetry and debug data. Hosted customers sometimes need extended controls for telemetry scrubbing or opt-outs, which is typical push towards Dedicated. Also some customers need region isolation and BYOK for full compliance.
[00:07:48] Daniel Herrera: Okay can we plan a pilot to validate SAML + SCIM provisioning and BYOK with a single payment-adjacent route?
[00:07:56] Alex Kim: Absolutely. Priya — we'll run a 1.5-hour pilot where we provision a test user in Lighthouse IdP, map groups to roles, and test key import and a log export to their S3.
[00:08:06] Priya Desai: Sounds good. We'll bring configuration docs and Terraform examples.
[00:08:12] Maya Lin: Cost — if we isolate pods for security, what's the overhead? We need a ballpark to plan budget.
[00:08:18] Alex Kim: Isolation and Dedicated capacity will increase cost; we'll provide an estimate. For small pilot, overhead is limited. For production, pricing varies by reserved capacity and retention windows. We'll include a delta for dedicated route isolation in the follow-up.
[00:08:31] Samir Patel: One last question: are you able to sign a CLA that covers our data processors and cert schedules?
[00:08:37] Alex Kim: We'll share our DPA and security addendum. Our legal team can discuss the CLA.
[00:08:44] Rina Ortega: Great. Thanks.
[00:08:47] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone — we'll send the SOC2 summary and questionnaire; Priya will schedule the pilot.
[00:08:55] Priya Desai: I'll follow up with the Terraform snippets and BYOK runbook.
[00:09:02] Daniel Herrera: Good meeting.
[00:09:05] Alex Kim: Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels came in as 'Speaker 1' and small transcription errors: 'KV cache' occasionally became 'KV cash' and 'SCIM' sometimes mis-transcribed. We'll attach the native recording and the security questionnaire as follow-up links.
